questions.q: What IS this feature in one sentence?
questions.a: Controls dust particle effects: footstep dust on terrain, dust accumulation on surfaces, and ambient dust density per biome type.

questions.q: What wider system does it belong to?
questions.a: The ground_terrain rung — dust VFX is a visual sub-system of terrain interaction, alongside footstep_response and grain_scale.

questions.q: What would break if this feature didn't exist?
questions.a: Footsteps would produce no visual feedback, ground surfaces would look sterile, and biomes would lack atmospheric particle density differentiation.

questions.q: What existing feature does this most resemble?
questions.a: footstep_response (audio) — dust_vfx is the visual counterpart. Also beacon_signal_vfx for particle system patterns.

questions.q: Is this a rung, a sub-rung, or a parameter?
questions.a: Sub-rung of ground_terrain, auto-decomposed from the parent constraint set.

questions.q: What physical constraint does it encode?
questions.a: Dust particle density per terrain type: sand produces 50 particles/footstep, rock produces 5, ice produces 0. Ambient dust density varies by biome (desert=0.8, arctic=0.2).

questions.q: What is the ONE measurement that proves it works?
questions.a: Footstep dust particle count per step matches terrain type within ±3 particles across 100 step samples on the same terrain.

questions.q: What wall must it never violate?
questions.a: Must never generate more than 500 particles per frame (performance wall). Must never occlude player vision with ambient dust (visibility wall).

questions.q: What would a degenerate winner look like?
questions.a: A winner with 0 particles on all terrain (feature invisible) or 10000 particles per step (unplayable particle fog).

questions.q: How would we know if the constraint is too loose?
questions.a: If sand and rock produce identical dust particle counts, the terrain-type differentiation constraint is too loose.

questions.q: At what scale does this feature operate?
questions.a: Per-footstep-event (every 0.5-1.5s during movement) and per-frame ambient (60fps continuous evaluation).

questions.q: What is the right definition level for this scale?
questions.a: Parameter-level: 4 variables (particles_per_step_terrain_map, ambient_density_per_biome, particle_lifetime_sec, dust_accum_speed).

questions.q: Could this be decomposed further? Into what?
questions.a: Could split footstep dust and ambient dust into separate sub-rungs, but 4 parameters cover both as a single Niagara system.

questions.q: At what resolution does the pattern emerge?
questions.a: Pattern emerges after 3-5 footsteps on a new terrain type — visual feedback tells the player 'you are walking on sand/rock/ice.'

questions.q: What would 'deep enough' look like for this feature?
questions.a: When terrain types are visually distinguishable by dust particle behavior alone (sand puffs, rock chips, ice crystals). Player can identify terrain by particle feedback without looking at the ground.

questions.q: What element catalog variables does this train?
questions.a: dust_particles_per_step, ambient_particle_density, particle_lifetime, dust_accumulation_rate.

questions.q: How many relevant elements exist in the catalog?
questions.a: 34 catalog entries tagged 'dust', 'particle', and 'vfx' — Niagara emitter templates and material parameters.

questions.q: Are there enough variables to train meaningfully?
questions.a: Yes — 4 parameters with 34 catalog elements provide solid constraint coverage.

questions.q: What variables are MISSING from the catalog?
questions.a: Per-weather-system dust modifiers (wind direction/speed should affect ambient dust density).

questions.q: Would training this require GPU acceleration?
questions.a: No — 4 variables is far below the 1000-variable GPU threshold.

questions.q: Does this feature connect to the Mirror of Erised?
questions.a: Indirectly — dust VFX makes the world feel physically real. A sterile world with no particle feedback reduces immersion, which dims the emotional weight of the Mirror signal.

questions.q: How directly does it serve the Mirror? (direct/enabling/orthogonal)
questions.a: Orthogonal — the Mirror works without dust particles. But haptic-visual feedback deepens immersion, which makes the Mirror's emotional signal land harder.

questions.q: Would a costless life still be meaningful without this feature?
questions.a: Yes — the Mirror's signal is emotional, not visual. Dust VFX is polish.

questions.q: Could this feature be gamed to fake a generous life?
questions.a: No — particle effects are purely cosmetic. No gameplay manipulation possible.

questions.q: What would this feature look like if it perfectly served the Mirror?
questions.a: Dust particles make the world feel physical and alive. Every footstep kicks up terrain-appropriate dust. The desert biome has a warm dust haze that catches the beacon's red light.

questions.q: What other features does this compose with?
questions.a: ground_terrain (terrain type mapping), footstep_response (event trigger), beacon_signal_vfx (light interaction with particles).

questions.q: What could break at the seam between this and its neighbors?
questions.a: footstep_response plays a hard-step audio on ice while dust_vfx emits zero particles on ice — audio and visual contradict each other.

questions.q: Does this need a decoder step to place in the level?
questions.a: No — dust VFX is a Niagara system on the player character, not a level-placed actor.

questions.q: What would a failed composition look like?
questions.a: Dust accumulation material shows 100% coverage on all surfaces because the accumulation_speed parameter ignored the biome density input from ground_terrain.

questions.q: Does this feature need a human judgment or can the system verify it?
questions.a: System verifies particle count per step and per-frame performance budget. Human judges whether the dust looks natural (golden-hour light scattering is a visual art choice, not a metric).

questions.q: How many generations to converge?
questions.a: ~50 generations at pop=32 for 4-parameter particle system.

questions.q: What population size is appropriate?
questions.a: 32 — small parameter space with discrete terrain-type mapping.

questions.q: What's the risk of overfitting?
questions.a: Low — 4 parameters with clear per-terrain-type constraints produce stable solutions.

questions.q: What's the risk of underfitting?
questions.a: Low — the parameter space is small and well-bounded by physical limits (min 0, max 500 particles).

questions.q: Does the existing trainer support this domain type?
questions.a: Yes — core.trainer handles particle-count constraints with per-terrain-type mapping objectives.

questions.q: Have we gone deep enough on this feature?
questions.a: Yes — 4 parameters for a visual polish sub-rung is adequate.

questions.q: What would the NEXT level of decomposition look like?
questions.a: Per-terrain-type dust material: separate Niagara emitters for sand (tan particles), rock (grey chips), and ice (white crystals).

questions.q: If we stopped here, would the game feel complete?
questions.a: Yes — dust VFX is a polish layer. The game plays the same without it but looks more alive with it.

questions.q: What is the human's expected emotional response to this feature?
questions.a: Tactile grounding — dust particles make the world feel physically responsive. Every step confirms the ground is real. Subtle but important for immersion.

questions.q: Does this feature exist because the Mirror demands it, or because it's technically interesting?
questions.a: Technically interesting — dust VFX is a visual polish feature. The Mirror would work without it, but the world would feel sterile.
